bullets.title: INTC: Worst day in 4+ decades on PC collapse + supply constraints; multiple downgrades
bullets.body: Intel fell 24-26% (worst day since 1974) after guiding 4Q revenue $15-16B vs Street $17B—a ~10% miss—on PC market deterioration (CY26 units -12%, CY27 -10%) and a $300M revenue hit from an Israeli fab explosion. Data Center/AI grew 78% YoY but was overwhelmed by the Client Computing collapse. BofA cut to Neutral ($100 PT), Roth Capital cut to Neutral ($70 PT), Seaport cut to Neutral; Citi maintains Buy but cut PT to $100 on revised estimates. 2027 flagged as negative FCF investment year. Foundry execution improving but constrained by Intel 3 supply and substrate availability through 1H27.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Largest T+1 earnings drop on record; Search misses, AI monetization headwinds
bullets.body: Alphabet fell ~12-13% post-earnings—its largest single-day post-earnings decline on record—as Search revenue grew only 12% vs 14-15% expected, with AI Mode queries driving lower monetization per search. Google Cloud grew 103% YoY but investors flagged lower-margin TPU sales (100 customers, significant COGS pressure) and $51.4B quarterly CapEx producing negative FCF. YouTube missed at +9% vs +13% expected. MS cut PT to $375 from $447 (maintain Buy); Citi cut to $375, reduced estimates. October MTD performance: GOOGL -18.7%.

bullets.title: AMZN: AWS guides 40%+ for 2027-28 above Street; retail/capex pressure stock -7%
bullets.body: Amazon AWS grew 39% in 3Q vs buy-side bogey of ~43%, but management guided 40%+ growth for both 2027 and 2028—the first time Amazon gave specific future-year guidance—targeting eventual $1T AWS revenue. AWS backlog surged $82B Q/Q to $578B. Q3 capex of $77.3B was 31.7% above consensus with meaningfully higher 2027 spend signaled. North America OI beat 8.5% but Q4 OI guide midpoint was $31B, ~6.6% below consensus, sending the stock -7% pre-market. Hedgeye upgraded to Top Long on the AWS acceleration thesis; JPM raises 2027 AWS estimates and OI projections.

bullets.title: MSFT: Azure +48% beats, guides +49-50%; FCF positive despite AI capex; $25B bond sale
bullets.body: Microsoft beat on all key metrics: Azure +48% YoY (Street ~44-45%), M365 Commercial Cloud +18%, gross margin 67.8%, operating margin ~50%. F2Q guidance for Azure +49-50% exceeded buy-side expectations. The company lowered 2026 capex guidance slightly to ~$170B due to third-party capacity delays while signaling FY27 step-up. MSFT also issued a $25B bond—its first IG debt deal since 2017—to fund AI infrastructure. GS raised PT to ~$700, MS raised PT. MSFT executing voluntary buyouts of ~60K employees (27% of workforce) to preserve margins.

bullets.title: RDDT: -36% weekly on search referral cliff; Google AI Mode cutting logged-out traffic
bullets.body: Reddit fell 36% over the week after 3Q results showed a 900K decline in US DAUs and Google Search referral traffic declining ~1M users/week in October, with management guiding potential low-double-digit Q/Q total DAU decline in 4Q. Ad revenue grew +54% YoY with 54% incremental margins, and click/conversion volumes accelerated, but the structural dependency on Google logged-out traffic is an acute risk. Citi maintains Buy but cuts PT to $186; Raymond James trims PT to $150 maintaining Strong Buy; multiple analysts flag the transition to fully logged-in platform as key 2027 execution risk.

bullets.title: NOW: -34% weekly; AI ACV raised but cRPO guidance disappoints
bullets.body: ServiceNow fell ~34% on the week after guiding 4Q constant-currency cRPO growth to 18.5% vs ~20% buy-side expectation. 3Q beat narrowly (sub revenue +0.2% above consensus) and AI net new ACV grew 65% YoY to $1.7B target, but professional services gross margins collapsed to -19.5% and subscription GM fell 300bps YoY for the fourth straight sequential decline. Stock had run ~60% since 2Q earnings, creating a high bar. Wolfe shifts to 'Duck and Cover'; most analysts maintain OW/Buy but trim PTs and patience.

bullets.title: CVNA: +18% weekly; SEC closes investigation, retail sales +39% YoY
bullets.body: Carvana surged 18% on the week, driven by the SEC closing its investigation with no enforcement action recommended and a strong 3Q26 print showing retail unit sales +39% YoY (~217K units), inventory up 30% to 87K units, and retail GAAP GPU improving 3% YoY despite fuel headwinds. Production capacity of ~1.5M annual units vs ~870K run rate provides significant headroom. Citi reiterates Buy at $90 PT; Morgan Stanley elevated to Top Pick. Stock also rose on easing of the AI capex narrative as a defensive play.

bullets.title: SNDK: Beat-and-raise; data center 50% of bits, AI-driven NAND sold out through decade
bullets.body: SanDisk reported September quarter revenue of $11.03B (+23% Q/Q, +37% YoY), beating guidance of $10.3-10.8B, with EPS $49.51 beating $46.67 consensus on 85.1% gross margins. F2Q guidance of $12.2-12.6B was ~10% above Street. ~50% of FY27 bits and 67% of FY28 bits are under NBM (Named Business Model) agreements, with the pipeline exceeding available supply through 2030. Management also announced an 8-for-1 stock split effective Nov 19. Citi and Mizuho maintain Buy/Outperform with Citi at $2,100 PT.

bullets.title: DASH acquires CART for ~$17B; JPM suspends ratings on conflict
bullets.body: DoorDash agreed to acquire Instacart for ~$17B (~$65/share, ~75% cash/25% stock), expected to close end-2027 or 1H28. The deal adds CART's 2,220+ retail partners and 26M annual orderers, accelerating DASH's Grocery & Retail business by years; Citi estimates $500M+ annual synergies net of investments. DASH 3Q Core orders grew 17% YoY, US restaurant GOV hit 5-year high. CART was repurchasing shares and generated $342M EBITDA in 3Q with 23% ad revenue acceleration. JPMorgan suspended ratings and price targets on both DASH and CART due to acting as financial advisor.

bullets.title: MRVL/LITE: Advanced M&A talks; all-stock deal at modest premium expected
bullets.body: Marvell Technology is in advanced discussions to acquire Lumentum Holdings in an all-stock deal at 'not all that large a premium,' with potential announcement as early as the week of Nov 3. LITE is sold out through 2028, growing 40-60% annually, and supplies critical narrow linewidth lasers for pluggable optics and CPO. Deal would vertically integrate MRVL's optical DSPs with LITE's photonics. MRVL fell ~11% on the announcement; LITE rose ~7-10%. Wolfe questions timing given LITE's strong FY31 guidance; MS rates MRVL Equal-weight citing peak cyclical conditions.

bullets.title: META: ~$97.5B equity raise clears AI capex overhang; NVDA/AMD/AVGO cornerstone investors
bullets.body: Meta priced ~$22.5B common via forward sales plus $12.5B mandatory convertible preferred, with NVDA investing $3B and AMD investing $1B. A $60B ATM program is planned for Q1 2027. The raise covers roughly half of the estimated $180-220B total funding need through 2028, with remainder expected as debt. 3Q META revenue grew 26.1% YoY to $64.6B, beating consensus by $1.3B, with Q4 guidance of $73-76B (+24.4% YoY at midpoint). 2026 capex narrowed to $135-145B. Hedgeye maintains Top Long Idea; stock down 15.2% for the month despite the raise.

bullets.title: ORCL: Investor Day lifts sentiment; $30B+ FCF by FY29, only $20B incremental capital needed
bullets.body: Oracle's AI World Investor Day provided significant clarity on funding: only ~$20B incremental capital needed through FY30 (vs prior consensus of ~$60B), with FCF turning positive in 2H FY28 and targeting $30B+ in FY29 vs prior consensus of -$1B. FY30 targets: revenue $225B+ (35% CAGR), operating margin 40%+, EPS $21+. Infrastructure RPO reached $664B (>90% infrastructure). Stock rallied 10-11% on the disclosure. Citi raises FY27/28 estimates; GS upgraded estimates. $664B RPO and vendor financing/customer prepayment model reduces upfront cash needs by ~50%.

bullets.title: EQIX: Record bookings, raises PT to $1,250; MS names Top Pick on 49GW power shortfall
bullets.body: Equinix reported record $533M gross bookings (+35% YoY) with 12% new deal pricing gains in 3Q, raising FY26 core FFO/share guidance. Morgan Stanley raised EQIX to Top Pick at $1,250 PT, citing a projected 49GW US power shortfall by 2028 and EQIX's unique colocation advantages. DLR also beat with record $627M bookings but MS maintains Equal-weight at $215 PT, citing equity dilution risk and preference for EQIX. Citi raised DLR PT to $234 from $226.

bullets.title: GLW: Strong 3Q optical beat; $220 PT, $40B revenue by 2030 target confirmed
bullets.body: Corning reported 3Q core EPS $0.91 (beat vs $0.88) on $5.08B revenue (+19% YoY), with optical segment growing 44% YoY and enterprise optical up 84%. Q4 guidance of EPS $0.96-1.00 and revenue $5.2-5.3B beat consensus. Management confirmed Springboard plan targeting $30B annualized revenue by end-2028 and $40B by end-2030. FCF of $661M dramatically exceeded the $274M consensus estimate. Citi maintains Buy at $220 PT; Wolfe Research raises PT following the beat.

bullets.title: VRT: +17% on record earnings; organic orders +100%, raises FY26 guidance
bullets.body: Vertiv beat 3Q revenue by 15% vs Street ($4.31B actual) with organic order growth exceeding 100% YoY and Americas orders +66%. FY26 guidance raised to revenue $14.45-14.85B and FCF $16-17B. Roth raises PT to $345; Goldman raises PT; management completed acquisitions of Utility Innovation Group and King Environmental. AI data center demand confirmation from VRT's print is widely seen as bullish read-through for the sector.

bullets.title: GEV: Beat/raise with $9B Trench Group acquisition; orders +96% organically
bullets.body: GE Vernova reported 3Q orders up 96% organically and raised FY26 guidance (revenue $46.5-47.5B, adj EBITDA margin 13.5-14.5%, FCF $16-17B). The company also acquired Trench Group for $9.0B at 13x 2028 adj EBITDA, expanding HVDC capabilities. GEV increased its buyback authorization from $10B to $20B. MS upgraded to OW from EW.

bullets.title: RBLX: 4Q EBITDA guide implies -10% to -15% bookings YoY; GTA VI risk flagged
bullets.body: Roblox 3Q26 bookings beat consensus by 4%, but 4Q bookings guidance of $1.89-2.00B missed the Street's $1.97B high end, and 4Q covenant Adj. EBITDA guidance of $320-380M was 12% below consensus. Age verification requirements and GTA VI launch (mid-4Q) are near-term headwinds. Citi lowers PT to $55 from $60 but maintains Buy; DA Davidson maintains Neutral at $54 PT citing 2-3 quarter near-term headwinds.

bullets.title: DKNG: NY OSB GGR +67% YoY in week ending 10/25; handle -7% but hold rate +510bps
bullets.body: DraftKings NY sports betting GGR grew +67% YoY for the week ending Oct 25 driven by hold rate expansion of +510bps to 11.6% from 6.5%. Handle declined -7% YoY but recovered +7% sequentially. October MTD GGR growth tracking +36% YoY with market share at 32.4%. UBS maintains Buy at $48 PT based on 17x 2028E EBITDA.

bullets.title: ENPH: -20% on 4Q guidance miss; solar demand weakness and margin pressure
bullets.body: Enphase reported 3Q EPS $0.41 (vs $0.51 consensus) and guided 4Q revenue to $225-255M, far below the $297.6M consensus, citing weak US residential solar demand and tariff/BESS margin pressure. SEDG fell ~10% in sympathy. Roth Capital and Oppenheimer both downgraded to Neutral/Perform. Mizuho cut 2027 revenue estimate by 14% to ~$1B. European sell-through declined -12% in 3Q.

bullets.title: FSLR: Q3 beat but cuts 2026 guidance; bookings inflection pushed to mid-2027
bullets.body: First Solar reported Q3 EPS $5.30 beating $4.67 consensus but cut 2026 revenue, EBITDA, volume sold, and capex guidance. US developers showing limited urgency to book 2029-2030 volumes due to financing, interconnection, tariff, and permitting issues. Post-Section 232 pricing reset is taking longer than expected. BMO lowered 2027 revenue estimate to $5.4B from $5.9B. GLJ Research downgraded to Hold ($161 PT). MS and Roth maintain Buy/OW but trim PTs. Board authorized $500M buyback.
